text:
incidentbot: :rotating_light: Alert: idp-heartbeat anomaly detected. 500+ auth heartbeats from 34.87.12.9 over 10m hitting /sso/callback. Potential token scraping + some debug logs forwarded to telemetry-s3-bucket. Flag: possible leaked JWT fragments.

alice.nguyen: oncall here, looking. can someone post sample log lines (sanitized) and which bucket objects were touched?

mike.security: I pulled a sample (redacted) — looks like truncated jwt==> `eyJhbGciOi...eyJzdWIiOjEw` in a debug field. Not seeing clear PII, but tokens could be abused.

sara.infra: confirmed telemetry-forwarder lambda wrote 3 objects in `s3://telemetry-raw/2026/03/17/`. listing now.

sara.infra: ```
aws s3 ls s3://telemetry-raw/2026/03/17/ --summarize
3 objects  1.2 MB
```

alice.nguyen: ok. initial triage: attacker IP is external, pattern is replay-ish. immediate mitigation options: block IP at WAF, rotate telemetry service principal creds, and quarantine + scrub the 3 objects.

mike.security: agree. priority: rotate service principal used by forwarder (svc-telemetry). Also rotate any short-lived tokens issued to clients if we confirm leakage. Notify PM teams about potential customer impact.

jay.cs: heads-up: one customer (tenant: acme-corp) has suspicious repeated 401->200 flows in their logs. need asap confirmation whether tokens visible belong to them. If so, we'll prepare a notification draft.

sara.infra: started WAF block rule for 34.87.12.9 (temporary). added rule id: wf-9921.

sara.infra: kicked off S3 object copy to quarantine bucket `s3://telemetry-quarantine/6112223333/` and set objects to private.

alice.nguyen: running key rotation now for svc-telemetry. posting commands/output: 
```bash
# create new key via secrets manager
aws secretsmanager create-secret --name svc/telemetry/key --secret-string "NEW_KEY_PLACEHOLDER"
# update lambda env + restart
aws lambda update-function-configuration --function-name telemetry-forwarder --environment Variables={API_KEY=NEW_KEY_PLACEHOLDER}
```

sara.infra: lambda env updated, invoked a test, forwarding rate back to normal.

mike.security: request logs scrub checklist: 1) Quarantine original objects 2) Create redaction copy (remove any tokens) 3) Replace raw objects with redacted versions or delete per retention policy 4) Audit who pulled those objects.

alice.nguyen: doing audit on S3 access logs now. quick grep shows `ec2-i-024` (internal processing host) downloaded object once. no external reads except the initial forwarder write.

mike.security: open ticket INC-6112 to track rotation + customer comms. Assigning to alice.nguyen (owner) and sara.infra (infra).

jay.cs: write me a 1-paragraph for legal/PM once we confirm tenant mapping. want to avoid alarming customers if no credentials leaked.

alice.nguyen: early customer-impact note: acme-corp has 12 auth events that correlate to the suspicious window. tokens appear truncated in logs; at this point I would say possible token exposure for a subset of sessions. recommending proactive rotation for their active client secrets and a customer-facing advisory if we confirm full tokens.

mike.security: we should also rotate internal signing key used for short-lived tokens if any risk of replay. can infra confirm if STS role was used?

sara.infra: STS assume-role logs show no external assume calls. only internal service role `role/telemetry-forwarder` used. rotating that principal now — updating trust policy and creating new key.

security-bot: automated scan completed: no known CVE triggered. flagged objects contain 5 truncated JWT-like strings.

alice.nguyen: action summary: 
- WAF block in place for 34.87.12.9 (sara)
- Telemetry service key rotated and lambda updated (sara)
- Raw objects quarantined; redaction in progress (alice + sara)
- Audit of accesses and mapping to acme-corp (alice)
- INC-6112 created for rotation + comms (mike)

mike.security: confirm timeline: aim to finish redaction + audit in next 2 hours, then decide customer comms. If tokens fully exposed, trigger customer secret rotation and a coordinated notice.

alice.nguyen: agreed. preparing a short ops bridge in 20m for handoff. Morgan (night oncall) will take post-bridge watch.

morgan.oncall: I'll take handoff. please put all runbook links and outstanding tasks in the ticket before bridge.

alice.nguyen: adding runbook links to INC-6112 now and tagging morgan. also attaching scrub script: 
```python
# redaction sketch
for obj in objects:
    data = s3.get(obj)
    data = re.sub(r"eyJ[A-Za-z0-9-_]+\.[A-Za-z0-9-_]+\.[A-Za-z0-9-_]+", "[REDACTED_JWT]", data)
    s3.put(redacted_obj, data)
```

sara.infra: scrub completed for 3 objects, redacted copies in quarantine, originals deleted per policy. S3 access logs archived to `s3://telemetry-audit/6112223333/` and locked for forensics.

mike.security: good. please attach hashes of original objects to INC-6112 for chain of custody.

alice.nguyen: done. hashes and access audit uploaded. final note for handoff: WAF block remains for 24h, service key rotated, quarantine + redaction complete, no evidence of external reads beyond initial forwarder write. acme-corp impact possible but limited — recommend contacting them with guidance to rotate client secrets as precaution.

morgan.oncall: taking it. will keep watch and escalate to security if any new anomalies. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
